claim: A 2026 APAC industry report on Southeast Asian influencer marketing reports campaign-spend shares for six markets but contains no measure of creator income, creator headcount, creator survival, or creator exit.
stance_target: The position that the absence of Southeast Asian creator-side quantitative evidence is structural: the region's dominant information producers are brand-buyer-facing agencies who measure where advertising money goes, not what happens to creators
scope_conditions: Audited absence across full text of AnyMind Group's 16 April 2026 summary of its State of Influence in APAC 2026 report; six SEA markets; no sample sizes or methodology disclosed for any figure
quoted_support: Influencer campaigns on TikTok surged from 28.35% in 2023 to 50.58% in 2025, highlighting the platform's growing role as the primary channel for product discovery.
numbers: TikTok campaign share 28.35% in 2023 to 50.58% in 2025

claim: Brand influencer spend concentrates on different platforms in each Southeast Asian market: Singapore Instagram 71%, Malaysia Instagram 48% and TikTok 44%, Thailand TikTok 66%, Philippines TikTok 64%, and Vietnam TikTok plus Facebook above 90%.
stance_target: The position that Southeast Asia is not a single creator market and that platform-specific Western findings on channel survival and payouts have no single SEA counterpart to be compared against
scope_conditions: Six SEA markets; 2026 report; shares of brand campaign investment or volume, not creator income; sample size and methodology not disclosed; vendor-generated from the firm's own campaign book
quoted_support: Singapore Instagram remains the dominant platform for influencer campaign investment at 71% compared to the rest. [...] Vietnam Influencer marketing thrives on a multi-platform ecosystem dominated by TikTok and Facebook, which together account for more than 90% of influencer campaign activity.
numbers: Malaysia Xiaohongshu >28% of Lifestyle & Home spend

claim: Southeast Asian influencer marketing is shifting to Cost Per Result pricing tied to measurable conversions, which transfers campaign performance risk from brands onto creators.
stance_target: The position that structural changes in how SEA creators are paid are altering income volatility in ways no longitudinal dataset is tracking
scope_conditions: Southeast Asia; 2026; vendor assertion with no supporting measurement
quoted_support: This shift is reflected in the growing adoption of Cost Per Result (CPR) models, where influencer budgets are directly tied to specific campaign outcomes.
